subject: Derivative entitlement — operational playbook and redline clarifications
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Park <jill.park@omnicloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Derivative entitlement — operational playbook and redline clarifications

Jill,

Thanks again for sending the MSA redline. We reviewed OmniCloud's suggested edits and have three areas where we need immediate clarification before routing back to legal:

1) Derivative/Output Ownership carveouts — your draft appears to limit our ability to serve customer-generated outputs back to the same customer when those outputs are used in productized features (e.g., search index generation, suggestion models). Can you confirm whether OmniCloud intends a full assignment for any customer-provided content, or a more limited license for productization that preserves Redwood's right to operate runtime services?

2) Training and retrain restrictions — Section 5.2 restricts training on customer content unless separately authorized. For operational reasons we need a scoped feedback license that allows ephemeral use for online learning (e.g., improving suggestions within that customer tenancy) without enabling cross-customer model retraining. Is OmniCloud comfortable with a scoped, nonexclusive feedback license limited to: (a) tenancy-scoped online improvements, (b) aggregate, de-identified model tuning for Redwood-internal infra performance, and (c) explicit opt-out for model retrain?

3) Telemetry & evidence — procurement is asking for a data provenance matrix and evidence that we can segregate customer content at runtime (KV cache, prefix caching, model pinning). Please point us to the artifact you want to see and whether OmniCloud requires third-party attestation (SOC2 Type II) to accept scoped training language.

I'll loop in Laura and Ben for legal/ops commentary. We can schedule a 30-min sync next week to walk through the proposed language.

Thanks,
Michael

--
Michael Grant
Head of Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: derived_content_examples.pdf (examples of productized outputs), data_provenance_matrix.csv (runtime segregation matrix)

From: Jill Park <jill.park@omnicloud.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: OmniCloud Legal <legal@omnicloud.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@omnicloud.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 08:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Derivative entitlement — operational playbook and redline clarifications

Michael —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers from our side:

1) Productization vs assignment: OmniCloud's intent is to avoid an open assignment of customer IP. Our redline aims to prevent Redwood from asserting ownership over customer data in perpetuity. That said, we are open to a narrowly scoped license that permits running product features for the same customer and limited conversions (e.g., generating indexes or summaries for that customer's instance) — but not for general commercial use across OmniCloud customers.

2) Training carveouts: We can accept a scoped feedback/license model where Redwood may use customer content for tenancy-scoped improvements and for ephemeral online adjustments, provided: (i) model checkpoints used for cross-tenant retraining are not populated with raw customer content; (ii) any aggregated tuning uses de-identified, low-risk signal only; and (iii) customers are given an opt-out checkbox during onboarding. We'll ask legal to propose precise language.

3) Evidence: OmniCloud procurement requires a runtime segregation and evidence pack. That should include: an architecture diagram (how caches & KV are isolated), a mapping of logs/telemetry retention, and a confirmation on encryption key control (KMS). SOC2 Type II is sufficient for the procurement team; if Redwood can provide an attestation + the segregation artifact we should be able to move forward.

I'll have our counsel draft tightened language around the scoped license (takes 1-2 business days). Can we get the data_provenance_matrix.csv updated to show which artifacts are accessible to ops vs. models vs. export?

Best,
Jill

--
Jill Park
Head of Legal Operations | OmniCloud
jill.park@omnicloud.com

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Derivative entitlement — operational playbook and redline clarifications

Team — forwarding Jill's reply. Action items below (short timelines because procurement is pushing a Jan go/no-go):

- Laura: can legal draft the scoped feedback license language that matches Jill's three bullets? We should explicitly carve out: tenancy-scoped online updates, de-identified aggregated tuning for infra performance, and a documented opt-out. Please add a short operational definition for "ephemeral" (we propose 7 days cache TTL for online learning checkpoints unless customer opts in to longer).

- Ben: please update data_provenance_matrix.csv to include columns: artifact, accessible_to (ops/models/exports), retention_days, encryption_scope (customer_kms/shared). I attached the current CSV — can you produce an annotated version by EOD Tue?

- Neha: coordinate with SOC/compliance to bundle the SOC2 attestation + architecture diagram. Procurement wants the artifact bundle in one packet.

I'll set a 30-min sync for Tue 11am PT to review language before it goes to OmniCloud legal.

Thanks —
Michael

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Derivative entitlement — operational playbook and redline clarifications

Michael / Ben —

Thanks — I reviewed Jill's summary and propose the following draft points for the scoped feedback license:

• Scope: Nonexclusive, worldwide license to use Customer Content solely to (a) provide the Service to that same Customer; (b) perform tenancy-scoped online improvements (no export of raw customer content to cross-tenant training pipelines); and (c) create aggregate, de-identified telemetry for infrastructure tuning and performance improvements.

• Prohibitions: No model checkpoint or weight updates used for cross-customer model retraining shall contain raw or identifiable Customer Content. No assignment of Customer IP to Redwood.

• Opt-out: Customer may opt out of both (b) and (c) at onboarding; Redwood will implement opt-out flags which set retention TTLs and disable inclusion in aggregate datasets.

• Operational definition: "Ephemeral" learning artifacts = ephemeral in-memory checkpoints or cache entries with TTL <= 7 days; any longer persistence requires explicit customer consent and documentation in the procurement packet.

I'll draft a redline snippet for Section 5.2 and parallel language for the order form. Ben — once you update the CSV, I will attach the annotated language and we can send the packet to OmniCloud legal.

Laura
